label: Confirmed Deaths
contestNote: Held at 331 across every UNGRD balance since Aug 25, including the Sept 7, 06:30 report — the toll has now stayed flat for two weeks.

label: Injured
contestNote: UNGRD's Sept 7, 06:30 balance revised injured down slightly to 4,505, from 4,519 in the Sept 3 balance.

label: Missing
contestNote: UNGRD's Sept 7, 06:30 balance narrowed missing further to 111 — down from 122 on Sept 3 — as identification work continues.

label: Families Affected
contestNote: UNGRD's Sept 7, 06:30 balance recorded 466,709 people affected across 296,738 families in 498 municipios and 16 departments — up from 293,743 families on Sept 3, even though the people-affected total is roughly flat.

label: Structures Destroyed
contestNote: UNGRD's Sept 7, 06:30 balance cited 36,326 homes destroyed (a slight downward revision from 36,336 on Sept 3) and 202,002 damaged (up from 201,010), across 498 municipios, with 743 buildings collapsed.

label: Departments Affected
contestNote: Holding at 16 departments and 498 municipios in UNGRD's Sept 7 balance, unchanged since Sept 3; which department was added beyond Decree 1261's original 15 remains unclarified.

label: Reconstruction Cost Estimate
contestNote: A joint UNDP-UNGRD damage assessment published Aug 30 put total direct physical damage at COP 42.1 trillion (2.3% of GDP) — COP 37.4T in housing and COP 4.8T in health, education and community infrastructure — up from the government's earlier COP 30T preliminary estimate. Independent estimates still range from Oxford Economics' $1–2B to USGS's ~$40B (7% of GDP).

label: Aftershocks Recorded
contestNote: New shallow aftershocks continue near the epicentral zone — a M3.7 tremor near Andagoya on Sept 6 and a M3.0 event near Istmina on Sept 7 — though SGC has not published an updated running total since 325+ (Aug 17).

label: Chocó 'Plan Marshall' Reconstruction Pledge
contestNote: COP 2T private-sector pledge + COP 1T government infrastructure package, announced at the Sept 7 Quibdó business summit. Several English-language outlets initially overstated the government's COP 1T share as 'US$1 billion' (actually ~$320M) — a 'billón' translation error corrected by Rio Times Online on Sept 8.
